subject.title: Plugin `message_sending` hooks silently bypassed on channel agent-reply delivery paths (2026.5.26, still present in 2026.6.1)

question: Which fix scope should be canonical for this issue: the broad dispatcher plus Telegram streamed-final repair, or a narrower dispatcher-only fix with streaming tracked separately?
rationale: Current main is still broken, and the open PRs differ on whether Telegram preview-finalized delivery and exactly-once safety-hook semantics belong in the same fix; automation should not choose that product/security boundary by itself.

options.title: Repair Broad Canonical Branch
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 as the canonical path after rebase, suffix/duplicate-hook repair, and refreshed Telegram proof.

options.title: Land Narrow Dispatcher Fix First
options.body: Choose a smaller dispatcher-composition PR first, accepting that preview-finalized Telegram replies remain open work on this issue or a linked follow-up.

options.title: Pause For Unified Boundary Design
options.body: Defer the PRs into the broader outbound-policy discussion if maintainers want a single architectural boundary before changing channel-specific behavior.

recommendation.title: Repair Broad Canonical Branch
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93216 as the canonical path after rebase, suffix/duplicate-hook repair, and refreshed Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant decision point is the dispatcher/plugin-hook boundary from PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82823, which `steipete` merged and co-authored.
